# Chapter Fourteen: Necrosis

> *"The Specter of death is not to be feared by one who has lived wisely"*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

Two silhouettes entered the small hamlet of riverside, the dull roar of the rapids from the nearby fork of the yanshin river drowning out the furtive exchange of words between the two robed figures. “Why are we going into a town Maelen, you said we should avoid them” Marcus hissed at the old mage as the two took tentative steps towards their destination.

“Because there is someone here, we need to talk to, we have been out of touch, and I have to know what’s happening before we can plan our next move” he whispered.

The hairs on the back of Marcus’s neck rose with each step, this feels wrong, very, very wrong he thought scanning the small town, the sun had descended past the buildings an orange hue bathing the streets and structures, they passed quickly between the long shadows cast by the buildings, where are the people he thought nervously scanning the dark streets and empty buildings.

It was as if the residents had simply left, there wasn’t a sound or light in the entire hamlet.

Unlike the towns that Marcus was used to, this was much less rural with its narrow carriage cobblestone streets and rowhouses, in fact it gave Marcus the feeling of walking through pre–Victorian England he reflected to himself, his eyes roving to every dark corner he saw.

Marcus stopped and pointed to a wooden sign that hung halfway up the market street, the sign simply reading “Crystal Smith”.

Marcus nodded; he had assumed they were here to see the local mage, so the destination was of no surprise. Stepping past an alley the two froze in their tracks as a mournful wail echoed through the street, playing back and forth.

“What the hell was that?” Marcus whispered crouching by the building they had been walking by, trying his best to sidle up to the shadow of the structure as he carefully followed the ridgeline of the roofs, looking for movement, Maelen crouched next to him “I don’t know, but whatever it is, was north of here” he responded.

With a nudge both men hurried towards the wooden sign while keeping alert for any movement.

They reached the door a moment later, Marcus catching movement out of the corner of his eye in one of the alleys across the way, when he turned to look it was gone.

But still he had the feeling of being watched, squinting he tried to pierce the obsidian wall of shadow to no avail. Maelen pounded on the old wooden door sending crashing boom’s resounding over the street and causing the younger man to jump.

“Next time, warn me” Marcus hissed giving Maelen an annoyed look. The older man gave him an apologetic look and slammed the side of his fist against the door three more times.

Before he could raise his hand to do it again a baritone whisper barked from behind the door “Who is there?” it barked, Maelen leaned in, putting his mouth as close to the door as he could.

“A friend of Zathris” he said as low as he could while estimating that the man could still hear him through the door. There was a long pause and then Marcus could hear the raking of metal across wood as latches were thrown.

The door opened slightly, and a large hand emerged “You need to hurry, get in now” hissed the baritone voice and both men scrambled in.

The room was completely dark and what little light there was, came through the door which rapidly closed as Marcus heard the latches re-engaged.

A small lantern began to glow steadily, casting only enough illumination to light the small stone alcove the three occupied.

Marcus turned to find a large bull of a man with a shining bald head, despite the lack of hair he could tell this man was at least sixty but kept himself in excellent shape judging by his bulging forearms.

The man turned and cast an angry look at the two, he was obviously not happy to see them. “What in Mephis’s ass are you doing here?” the deep voice whispered at them, his suspicious glare moving between both men. Maelen seemed taken aback by this, obviously not used to the tone or greeting. “We came for sanctuary and intelligence, what’s wrong Blavin, don’t you recognize a fellow archivist?” he asked his own tone annoyed.

The large man leaned in squinting to get a better look under the cowl of the robe Maelen wore, after a moment he smiled shaking his head “Maelen, you old dog” he began and then the smile fell from his face, replaced with a look of resigned fear “You shouldn’t have come, this city is a grave yard, you have both signed your own death warrants” he said, moving past the two and walking up the aisle.

Stunned neither man moved for a moment, but as the light of the lantern diminished, moving with the large mage towards the back of the shop, both men moved simultaneously trying to stay within the weak light cast by the crystal lantern.

They quickly caught up with the large mage as he shambled past the counter and into the back of the small shop, once all three had walked into the back room the large man closed the heavy wooden door behind him, again Marcus heard latches click. This man was scared enough to not only lock the front door, but also this one as well Marcus thought as a chill ran down his spine, recalling the call wail from earlier.

“Blavin, what is going on?” Maelen asked once the man had turned to face the two of them. Marcus could see the signs of fear and stress written all over the mages face, judging by the dark circles under his eyes, this man had not slept in days.

“Oh Maelen, you picked a piss poor time to show up, the Black Queen is what happened my friend, her demons roam the town, over half the residents are dead, those of us remaining, are living on borrowed time” Blavin said, his tone that of a man resigned to his fate.

He moved past the two and set the lantern on a shelf, turning it up the two men could see the cache of supplies strewn about, he had obviously been living here for a while. “Demons?” Maelen asked his tone careful, as you would to one you suspected of having a mental breakdown. Blavin shot him an angry look. “I am not mad Maelen” he began and then sighed, the anger leaving his face only to be replaced by exhaustion as he reached into a box and pulled out salted port, offering some to the two mages, both accepted graciously.

“I better start from the beginning” he answered settling into a chair and motioning to two more empty seats, Maelen and Marcus shrugged out of the oversized cloaks they had used to hide their identity, and each took a seat, neither man relaxing as they waited for the shop keeper to tell his tale.

Blavin stared for a time at the lantern, his eyes were vacant of emotion as he collected his thoughts, trying to decide where to start, finally he turned back to his fellow mages and leaned in, Maelen and Marcus followed suit.

“About a week ago a contingent of soldiers moved into Riverside, they were led by a strange looking man who called himself one of the Empress’s chosen, he claimed he was to replace the current Lord Seer and that all people would be stripped of their property and put to work for the Kingdom” he began and paused allowing the two men to exchange alarmed glances.

“We had heard rumors about such things in other villages and towns but had not been able to confirm them” Marcus said, thinking of a farmer they had run into who told a similar story, not more than a week prior. Blavin nodded “it’s true, from what information I have received from the Order, it’s happening in all twelve major regions, but I digress” he continued. “Anyway, the residence would not stand for it, Lord Seer Homus is a good honorable man and one who has led us well. First the nobles came to his aid, threatening to peddle there influence and making threats, this Seer simply laughed Maelen, he laughed at these highborn and then with a wave of his hand turned their skin black, as if they had simply come down with a plague, dying in a moment right before our eyes” he continued and his gaze was haunted Blavin recalled the events of that day, Marcus knew that image would be seared into the man’s mind for decades.

“I have never seen power like this my friend, they had abilities I have only ever heard of, there skin was covered in runic script, actually embedded into their skin” he whispered and Maelen shot bolt upright at the mention of this. “Describe what you saw Blavin, please” he whispered.

The shopkeeper sighed recalling the details of the monstrous figure. “He wore a large black cloak, but every ounce of exposed skin had these runes that looked as if they had been carved directly into his skin, the areas around the runes were scarred and angry, and his eyes Maelen, were as black as his soul, I have never seen anything like it” he finished looking at his friend, pleading with him to explain what couldn’t have possibly existed.

Maelen slumped in his chair shaking his head “Nothing I say will answer, explain or help, please continue and leave nothing out” he whispered and Blavin nodded resigned.

Marcus kept an eye on Maelen, he knew something, and he would have to ask the old mage what that was, because whatever it was Marcus reflected, it had turned the old man sheet white with fear.

“As the nobles rotted right before our eyes and with that mage simply laughing at the sight of it, the residence panicked, everyone running for shelter. I ran to my shop, turning I watched as the man stood down his guard, I expected he would simply send the soldiers in to arrest the town, but he didn’t, he strolled up the main street and then he spoke, using magic to amplify his voice Maelen, it resonated throughout the town, vibrating the buildings as he spoke” Blavin paused, wiping his brow with a cloth, taking a single shaking break he braced himself to continue as the two mages sat on the edge of their seat.

“Everyone cowering in their homes heard him, he simply said this town is dead, you all are now dead, as I watched two of the young lads, strong lads came from their houses with knives and ran at the Seer, he simply waved a hand in their direction and they rotted, skin turning black and vomiting blood, within three steps they were on their knees, another foot and there skin was dissolving off of their bones, in front of the boy’s mother the seer walked over to the bodies, laughing as he plucked one of the boys skulls and using a quarterstaff blade, like we carry Maelen, they even had our weapons for Aurtus’s sake he sliced it in half, then put it on like a mask.”

He paused again and both men could see the tears freely rolling down his cheeks as he recalled the horror.

“That poor woman wailed for hours until her voice ran out, that was a week ago, since then the Seer strolls the streets and when he is not, his demons do, they are like nothing I have ever seen Maelen, they walk like men but they are twisted, beyond imagining, they are truly what demons would be limbs a little too long with sharp claws on their hands and feet, there head is slightly elongated to make way for large fangs, and the eyes glow Maelen, they grow RED” he said almost squealing that last part and the older mage stood up laying a hand on the man’s shoulder.

“It’s okay Blavin, what word from the outside, what of the Order and the territory as a whole” Maelen asked, partly because he needed the information and partly to distract the bigger man who sat like a scared child just awoke from a nightmare.

Blavin looked up at Maelen blankly for a moment but something in Maelen’s steel blue eyes brought him back and life returned to the blank stare that was his world a moment before.

“The Keep and the knights are gone, the Empress has destroyed the church and slaughtered more than half the messengers, the Order still stands but there are rumors the Wardens will be disbanded, Maelen the order has voted, they say the Empress has broken the agreement, but there is a stalemate on what to do, some want to go to war against the tyranny, but the Empress has support on the council, some are trying to convince the Order to surrender to the Empress, to serve her” he said.

Maelen withdrew his hand looking shocked at his friend “No, they can’t” he simply whispered as Blavin nodded, the blank stare returning.

Nodding towards Marcus the older mage stepped away from his friend, who now sat catatonic, his emotions and mind spent from the stress of the last week.

The two men stepped over to the corner of the room ensuring to keep their voices low as not to disturb the shopkeeper who simply sat, still staring blankly “What the hell is this about runes in the skin Maelen, I saw your face, you know something” Marcus asked and the older man nodded solemnly.

“Old forbidden experiments, sounds like the Empress has found access to things best left forgotten, if she has Marcus, we are in for a world of hurt, those are mages enhanced with Runes, I have no idea how strong they are or what they are capable of, the creatures though, I have heard of them in some of the archives it tells of the failed experiments and things called Crystal Wraiths or screamers for the sound they make, they are like walking animals with a lust for blood, we need to get out of here and fast” Maelen said.

Marcus could see the fear in his eyes, it took everything he had to keep his calm and with a few deep breaths he steeled himself, Marcus wouldn’t leave these people, would not allow this creature to kill them for sport, he had spent the better part of the trip questioning his own morality, yes he had killed and done so in cold blood, but for the first time since Orah’s death he found himself set on a purpose and one he could live with. “Maelen, I will not leave these people to their fate, these things are mages and it is going to take mages to deal with them, I need your help but dammit if I have to I will face them alone, I will not run from this, these people are innocent and need our help” Marcus said his words like a slap in the face for his friend.

Maelen winced and lowered his eyes for a moment, then with a nod he met his friends eyes “Your right, but understand, I don’t know if we can survive this Marcus, if you do this, we very well could end up dead or if they take us alive, worse” he said, his stare telling Marcus what he didn’t want to hear. If they try and take you, make sure your no longer living, those eyes said. The front door of the shop opened slowly revealing the cobblestone street, moonlight played over the buildings offering enough light to see.

As Marcus stepped out, he watched the shadows nestled between the buildings, scanning for any movement or signs of hidden enemies as the two men stepped out into the middle of the small market street. The town was a silent as a tomb the echoes of their footfalls shattering the stone silence as they stepped towards the town center.

Closing his eyes Marcus reached out, playing his consciousness out into the night, scanning for any sign of animal or man, as they slowly walked everything was still, like a calm before a storm.

Marcus stopped dead as his mind played over something cold and alien, the images made no sense as rapid fire graphics assaulted his senses like a macabre snuff film, holding up his hand he stopped Maelen.

Closing his eyes he reached out, concentrating, focusing on the insane rhythm of the thoughts slamming into the barrier of his mind. Finally, it became too much, and he pulled back, but not before an ear-splitting shriek erupted over the town, the echo’s sounding like responses.

“Maelen, I don’t know what these things were, but they aren’t human any longer, those images” he began and shuddered when trying to describe them. Marcus focused on his friend and noticed that he wasn’t looking at him, in fact he just stood there, his eyes wide, Marcus followed his gaze up the street and then saw what had his friend transfixed with fear, standing in the center of the narrow road, not more than a hundred feet from where they stood three figures loomed.

The one in the middle was unmistakably the Seer, he still wore the front shell of the young man’s skull, combined with the black cloak he looked like a spectral demon, but it was the creatures on either side that caught Marcus’s breath in his throat. They were almost human, but like the shopkeeper had described, they had been twisted, perverted somehow.

Marcus could see energy playing over the runes on all three, the magic twisting and wrenching as if someone had forced it with their will to bend in ways it was never supposed to. Marcus could not understand what he was looking at and before he could ask, the three creatures began moving forward towards them.

A deep laugh boomed over the town; he is enhancing his voice with magic Marcus thought listening as the concert level voice seemed to come from all around them.

“Mages, you will submit to my will and that of my Empress, you will serve, or you will die” the booming voice said as the three creatures slowly moved down the street closing the gap.

Out of the corner of his eye Marcus watched as his friend pulled the odd quarterstaff from his back, except this time he didn’t extend it, instead with a twist of the center the staff came apart into two short swords, the blades engraved with runes that began to glow as Maelen infused it with power. “I will take the Seer, can you handle the demons?” he asked and looking at his friend, his teacher he could see the worry and doubt.

Marcus had very little training, very little experience and he was about to match his will against creatures that had been twisted with the same magic he used.

He doesn’t think I will stand a chance” he thought as a lance of fear split through his psyche, with a force of will he shoved it down, he had no choice, he was the only thing standing between these perversions of magic and the innocent people now cowering in their homes.

They might be allowing them to come out a few at a time and hunting them for sport, but they would get bored, they would eventually simply go house to house tearing people apart Marcus thought and the fear was replaced with Rage.

“Do not fret my friends, it is just us, my soldiers have gone on to scout the next village, we have some quality time before they get back, I expect by the time they return I will have new acolytes for my Empress or a few new skulls for my collection” the Seer boomed as the three continued to move towards them.

Marcus began to collect power to himself, pulling like he had never pulled before feeling the energy collect until he felt as if he would explode. “Wait for my signal” Maelen whispered next to him and Marcus held the magic, it was like trying to hold your breath, the longer you held it, the worse it got until it felt as if he himself was on fire, but he held on, concentrating on not letting go of the power. Maelen stood there for two more agonizing minutes, allowing the three to get closer, with a flourish he reversed the blades, bringing them to rest against the bottom of his forearm and then with a burst of will, the old mage seemed to teleport across the distance, appearing directly in front of the Seer, for a moment the man stopped, surprised, but he had also pulled out his own staff and as Maelen went in for a killing blow, the two blades spun from under the robe, the silver runed blades glinting in the moonlight as they sliced and parried, the two men locked in a vicious dance of death.

Before the two demons could move in to assist Marcus thrust out his hands and with a bellow of rage released the power, the two creatures were caught off guard, both flung back almost the distance they had come, only to be brought up short by a thick stone wall on the side of the tavern. The satisfying sound of cracking stone and breaking bones echoed over the alleyway followed by screams of rage and pain.

Quickly pulling in energy Marcus thrust his palms downward and behind him, sending him flying through the air, he extended his arms sending light pushes of kinetic force against the buildings to steady himself. As he came near the ground, he expended the rest of the energy into a soft landing thrusting his hands down and in front of him.

Marcus had no weapons, but he had power, natural power that had not been twisted and bent and he once again pulled in energy, but before he could replenish, one of the creatures shrieked, pushing its palms at Marcus as two fireballs shot forward, Marcus dove left and felt the heat of the fireballs singe the leather of his outfit. As he landed, he gathered heat in his mind and pushing his will at the closest creature he watched as it ignited into a pillar of flame and smoke, its energy expended and unable to gather enough for a defense. A malicious smile spread across Marcus’s face, lit against the burning creature as it thrashed, trying to put out the flames.

He was so caught up in the first creature he almost didn’t see the second one launch itself over his brethren and come barreling down towards Marcus teeth bared and claws extended. It hit him while he was still on the ground and four sets of razor-sharp claws raked the front of the leather Mage armor, Sparks of energy flew from the leather as the armor spell held.

With a prayer of thanks to whomever had created it Marcus struggled with the creature, he grabbed both wrists, but the creature extended his arms, lowering himself towards the mage as his jaws snapped closed just inches from his face.

Looking into the red glowing coals the creature had for eyes, this thing did look like a creature from hell he thought, straining to hold on as he desperately tried to keep the thing from biting or clawing him, if the armor spell failed, of that thing managed to get those claws onto exposed skin, Marcus was done for he thought, panic welling up in his mind, with an effort he forced it down, gathering power once again.

He thought desperately trying to find something he could do or effect to get this thing off him, it wrapped its legs around his torso, ensuring Marcus couldn’t push it off with magic, he also couldn’t set it ablaze unless he too wished to join it. These things could reason, they could analyze a problem and come up with a solution he thought, not a mindless creature he realized and chided himself for underestimating the thing. He struggled with the thing for what seemed like an eternity, his muscles straining against the creatures own as they fought for position.

Marcus tried to get a look to see if Maelen might aid him, but when he looked, he could see his friend, sliced and bleeding as he was retreating from the Seer, the bone clad man advancing on his friend, it wouldn’t be long thought Marcus until Maelen would be dead, that thing was younger and faster and matched the old man in power.

As he lay there struggling, desperately trying to figure a way out, a way to help himself and his friend before they both wound up dead, or worse, he thought of the rabbit, the first one he had tried to influence, pushing too hard had killed the creature his mind locked onto something the old man had said Creatures changed by crystals are susceptible to manipulation, we can influence them and read their thoughts.

Marcus remembered the staccato of images, gathering his power, knowing he had one chance, should this fail he would die and so would Maelen.

Gathering every ounce of collected energy, Marcus pictured a razor-sharp lance and with all his will he pushed it directly into the creature’s head and slamming his own will into that of the demon.

The creature tensed, its thrashing stopped, then it began to convulse as Marcus pushed even more power into that lance DIE he willed pushing even harder, he felt himself beginning to ebb, beginning to weaken as darkness closed in around him, threatening to render him unconscious, but still he pushed harder, willing the last scraps of energy he had summoned into that things skull.

It stumbled off of Marcus and as he watched, it bled from its eyes and nose and mouth, it took a few staggering steps away from the young mage and collapsed, its head exploding into a mass of brain and blood.

Marcus rose to his feet unsteadily, his body on the verge of exhaustion. Turning he found the Seer still advancing on the retreating Maelen, he could see the things runes began to glow as it gathered power to himself.

Marcus was spent, he didn’t have the energy or the will to summon power, for a moment he stood there helpless, I need power he pleaded to his body and for a moment he was resigned to stand there watching in horror as Maelen was about to be annihilated.

“I’m an asshole” he whispered, damn near slapping his head. Taking the last of his strength he ran full speed at the Seer, the thing so focused on the kill, he didn’t even sense him coming, as he was within a few feet of the taller man, Marcus launched himself feet first bringing both of his heels against the Seers back and pushing. The Seer stumbled, surprised as he began to fall forward, the power released as his concentration was lost.

Maelen was quick, taking advantage of the moment of distraction he thrust both of the short blades into the Seer’s torso, as Marcus watched the ends emerged from his back, pulling them out Maelen gathered energy and using a kinetic push, spun three hundred and sixty degrees before the Seer could recover.

Its head jumped to the left of his body, falling to the ground with a meaty sound as the body stood there for a moment, as if unwilling to believe that the head was gone. Then it dropped to its knees for a long beat, before falling forward, dead.

Coming over to help his friend, the two Mages leaned on each other Maelen looking at the burning corpse of one and the exploded head of the other and smiled “I wouldn’t have thought of that” he said and Marcus elicited a tired chuckle, as they shambled back towards the Mages shop, doors began to open and people tentatively peaked their heads out, then they stepped slowly out of their houses, soon the streets were flooded with the survivors of the town.

**

The sun ascended above the stone shops, spreading light and warmth over the bloody streets, Marcus and Maelen stood, leaning on each other as they closed their eyes to the warmth of the coming morning.

“The soldiers will return, what do you think will happen?” Marcus asked looking back at the townsfolk, smiling as they checked on neighbors, some crying for lost friends or family.

Maelen turned to do the same “Not sure, maybe they will leave, the death of the Seer surely will give them pause” he began “If not, these people are still in danger” he finished.

“No, my friend, we are already distributing weapons, we will not allow the soldiers to enter this town, we no longer recognize the authority of the Black Queen” Blavin said approaching the two men.

He held two rifles, one of many he had handed out in the last few hours and stood smiling at the two mages “You two will always have a home here, with us” he said bowing slightly to them. Marcus lowered himself in an approximation of a bow until Vertigo forced him upright once again, Maelen begged off, but Marcus took the rifle with heartfelt thank you and then proceeded to check the eight-cylinder drum, Blavin handed him a satchel with two more drums and loose ammunition, the blue crystal spheres causing an ethereal glow against the inside of the leather bag. “Thank you Blavin, we were glad to help” Maelen answered.

Blavin’s face fell as he reached around his back and pulled another satchel, one that Maelen recognized, the emblem of the dragon emblazoned on the front of it. “These are all the missives that came in, as of this morning, a courier showed up in the early hours, I had a chance to review them, but you are not going to like it Maelen” he said and handed the satchel out for the other man to take.

Maelen took it, opening the top and pulling out a stack of parchment, standing here he began to slowly go through it as Marcus looked on, watching the other man’s face as he did. Maelen read fast at first and then slowing down as the missives progressed, finally once he had finished, lowering his head he put them gently back in the messenger bag and handed them back to Blavin “Keep them safe mage” he simply said and with a nod of understanding the other man turned and walked back towards the gathered townsfolk.

Maelen turned and began walking out towards the gate, the younger man following at first, he was silent but then his curiosity got the better of him. “What’s wrong Maelen, what did you see?” he whispered as they continued out of the small town. “The Empress has declared war on everyone, the Wardens are scattered the church is decimated and the Order is arguing whether or not to join her, Marcus, she has broken the agreement, if something isn’t done, war will break out”
